segments.text: The complex dot product is lesson one's kernel for radio samples, where every element is a real part and an imaginary part stored side by side.
Multiplying two complex numbers takes four products, one subtraction and one addition. Lane-wise SIMD multiplies only produce half of the products, in the wrong places.
SSE3 fixes that in three moves. First, duplicate the taps two ways, real parts into both lanes, then imaginary parts into both lanes.
Second, swap the sample pairs with a shuffle. Now every one of the four products exists, two per register.
Third, add sub. Subtract in the even lanes, add in the odd lanes, and the real and imaginary parts of the product come out already interleaved.
AVX is the same three moves at twice the width, four complex numbers per trip, with a scalar tail for the last zero to three elements.
AVX with FMA fuses the first multiply into the add sub.

NEON avoids the shuffle. A de interleaving load puts real parts in one register and imaginary parts in another, so the four products are plain lane-wise multiplies. NEON version 8 folds the subtraction into a fused multiply subtract.
